newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Iscor sees tough conditions in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Iscor sees tough conditions in 1996/97.

text.p: South African steel producer Iscor Ltd said it saw no immediate prospect of the domestic steel market improving and warned that profits in the first half of the 1996/97 year would be well down on a year ago.
"Despite the current market conditions, the company has set itself the objective of improving on last year's earnings of 26 cents a share," Smith added.
Iscor did not see an immediate upturn in the domestic market.
"We expect a further general decline in economic conditions and indications are that the international steel cycle has bottomed out although there may be a temporary recovery in 1997," Smith said.
He said the upper turning point of the local steel cycle was reached in August 1995.
"And the cycle continued downward to the end of the financial year, resulting in steel dispatches to the local market dropping by 12 percent to 2.86 million tonnes," Smith said.
Smith said exports accounted for 45 percent of total dispatches and were only one percent lower than the previous year.
"But the decrease in international steel prices during the second half of 1995 resulted in substantial reduction in average export dollar earnings," he said.
